title: Podcast: Why Sleep Beats Cramming
summary: Monólogo divulgativo — presente perfecto, conectores causales, léxico académico.
script:
Welcome back to the show. Today we're talking about something every student has tried at least once: staying up all night before an exam.
It feels productive, and that's exactly the problem. Research over the last two decades has consistently shown that sleep is not lost study time. It is part of studying.
During deep sleep, the brain replays what you practised during the day and moves it into more stable storage. If you skip that stage, much of what you reviewed simply does not stick.
One study compared two groups. Both learned the same list of words. One group slept normally; the other stayed awake. A week later, the sleepers remembered clearly more.
So what should you do instead? Study in shorter sessions across several days, and protect your sleep the night before. It is less dramatic than cramming, but it works.
That's all for today. See you next week.
